acceptance_status: Full automated-inventory checkpoint; full functional/native/manual/performance/release parity remains open.
scope: Preference branding/header/section/row/status copy and row/navigation backing use Rust scene recipes and one additional transparent Metal underlay. Native interactive/focus/AX and layout nodes remain adapters.

build_input_snapshot.gn_delta: No target/dependency change. Rust bridge adds clear_selection for existing SelectState. Explicit native adapters, preference selector allocation/refresh and browser tests changed. Concurrent root network-policy work remains excluded.
build_input_snapshot.method: Frozen UI overlay base a3afc206f742f0a59da6e65d609ddf1df3c7326d plus 16 explicit live UI overrides (including sidebar_metal.h/mm), with committed own installer/stager hooks; concurrent network-policy changes excluded. Twenty-one prototype source hashes are matched to committed, live and staged inputs.

native_service_patch.license: Generated Chromium header and source hook retain the Chromium BSD-style license; project adapter/tool/model changes use Apache-2.0.

additional_performance_scenario_coverage.purpose: Execute all four opt-in performance scenarios as additional automated coverage, with their default 30 trials. Metal validation is enabled; these are not controlled CPU/GPU/drawable presentation comparisons.

contracts: The Rust preference tree has no native Label instances. PreferenceCopy remains a native static-text accessibility/layout adapter, with text and exact weight rendered through Rust recipes and the Metal text cache.

Native gfx::ElideRectangleText long-word handling and TypographyProvider minimum line height preserve original Label geometry. Tests compare real title/hint heights against native Label at widths 80, 160 and 320; native font/Unicode shaping remains a platform adapter.

One shared preference chrome underlay renders clipped row/navigation backing and text. Rust subtracts the union of interactive control holes; actual Cocoa subview ordering puts the underlay below control canvases. Existing editor/control canvases remain separate.

Navigation retains CPU backdrop painting for control fallback. Row/text CPU recipes remain fallback when the shared canvas is unavailable. No claim of eliminating all CPU drawing or native views is made.

Dynamic Unicode error/status/profile labels, theme changes, no-results filtering, maximum scroll, full last-editor visibility, interactive cutouts, hide/reopen and underlay ordering pass. Prior preferences/editor/action/switch/selector/navigation and browser-service tests remain in the full matrix.
Native data stores, authorization, managed-setting checks, profile-bound confirmations and service commands remain unchanged. No new crate/library/dependency was added.

views_recheck.purpose: Retain original matrix teardown timeout; diagnose isolated case, then repeat complete Views matrix without retries or changed code.

views_timeout_note: Original full Views matrix had one timeout in NameEditorBidiDirectionAndSharedKillYank, with stack in PostRunTestOnMainThread/AppKit/FrontBoard teardown. Unchanged isolated test and complete Views matrix were repeated; initial failure retained. No claim that root cause is fully established.

initial_probe.issues: Initial Metal gate had four failures including typography mismatch, visibility, presentation and scroll assertions; Views passed eleven. Native line wrapping/minimum line height were restored and the final unchanged gate passed all 16/11. Earlier failures are retained, without claiming every timing failure has a proven single cause.

limits: Remaining UI descriptions/data and draft/admission/busy/form state, tools/provider pickers, other forms and browser-service panels, outer layout and native interaction/container ownership still require migration.
Manual IME/candidate-window, VoiceOver, complex bidi/RTL, pointer/trackpad, scale/theme, detach/reattach and GPU recovery acceptance remain open.
Default-30-trial optional scenarios provide execution coverage, not a controlled CPU/GPU/drawable-presentation speedup comparison.
Normal installed applications/profiles were untouched; no release bundle was packaged/signed. Final shipped-binary Apache-2.0/upstream license/notice acceptance remains open.
